claims.text: Coupling experimental phase diagrams with computational simulation results will enable better control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
The relevant initial material is an unprocessed Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloy.
Experimental phase diagrams can be integrated with computational simulation results.
The proposed method requires precise adjustment of temperature and composition in a controlled laboratory environment.
Phase diagrams represent the stability of different phases under varying conditions.
Integrating experimental data with computational models provides predictive insight into phase stability and phase transformations.
Predictive insight into phase stability and transformations facilitates targeted adjustment of processing conditions.
Targeted processing adjustments will enhance control over phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Enhanced phase-evolution control will lead to desired microstructural properties.
The proposed approach may not generalize beyond Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
The degree of improvement may vary with experimental conditions and alloy composition.
